key_insight: Under drift smoothness assumptions, Schrödinger–Föllmer samplers achieve total variation error bounds of O(h|ln h|) with exact drift and O(h|ln h| + 1/M) with Monte Carlo drift estimates.
engineering_relevance: These finite-time guarantees help guide time-step and Monte Carlo sample-budget choices for high-dimensional, multimodal sampling without relying on long-time ergodicity.
method: Analyze transport from a point mass at t=0 to the target distribution at t=1.
Use the Bismut–Elworthy–Li formula to derive Kolmogorov-equation regularization estimates.
Bound total variation error through weak-error analysis with non-smooth test functions.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments illustrate convergence with respect to time-step size h and Monte Carlo sample count M, alongside sampler effectiveness.
watch_item: The bounds require regularity assumptions; the improved 1/M dependence is measured in total variation, unlike the earlier 1/√M bound in L²-Wasserstein distance.
paper_title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
